definition_zh: 比喻做了多余的事，反而把事情弄糟。
definition_en: To ruin something by adding what is superfluous; to gild the lily.
example_zh: 这篇文章的结尾已经很完整，再加一段反而画蛇添足。
example_en: The ending of this article is already complete; adding another paragraph would only spoil it.

definition_zh: 比喻死守狭隘经验、不知变通，或抱着侥幸心理，妄想不劳而获。
definition_en: To wait idly for a windfall, trusting to chance instead of making an effort.
example_zh: 找工作要主动投简历，不能守株待兔，等着机会自己上门。
example_en: When job hunting, you need to send out resumes proactively instead of idly waiting for opportunities to knock.

definition_zh: 比喻出了问题以后想办法补救，可以防止继续受损失。
definition_en: To mend the fold after a sheep is lost; it is never too late to fix a problem.
example_zh: 这次考试没考好，亡羊补牢，从现在起认真复习还来得及。
example_en: You didn't do well on this exam, but it's not too late to make amends — start reviewing seriously from now on.

definition_zh: 比喻自己欺骗自己，明明掩盖不住的事情偏要设法掩盖。
definition_en: To deceive oneself by covering one's ears while stealing a bell.
example_zh: 问题摆在那里，假装看不见不过是掩耳盗铃。
example_en: The problem is right there; pretending not to see it is just deceiving yourself.

definition_zh: 比喻见识狭窄、眼界有限的人。
definition_en: A frog at the bottom of a well; a person with a very limited outlook.
example_zh: 多出去看看世界，别做井底之蛙。
example_en: Go out and see the wider world; don't be a frog at the bottom of a well.

definition_zh: 比喻拘泥于成例，不知道随着情境的变化而改变看法或方法。
definition_en: To carve a mark on the boat to look for a sword lost in the river; to act on outdated assumptions.
example_zh: 情况已经变了，还用老办法就是刻舟求剑。
example_en: Things have changed; sticking to the old approach is like carving a mark on the boat to find a lost sword.

definition_zh: 比喻表面上爱好某种事物，实际上并不真正爱好。
definition_en: Like Lord Ye, who claimed to love dragons but fled from a real one; to profess a love one does not truly feel.
example_zh: 他总说喜欢冒险，真要去跳伞时却退缩了，真是叶公好龙。
example_en: He always says he loves adventure, but when it came to skydiving he backed out — a real case of Lord Ye's professed love of dragons.

definition_zh: 比喻依仗别人的权势来欺压、吓唬人。
definition_en: Like the fox borrowing the tiger's terror; to bully others by borrowing someone else's power.
example_zh: 他没有什么本事，不过是狐假虎威，借着领导的名头吓唬人。
example_en: He has no real ability; he just borrows the boss's authority to intimidate others, like the fox behind the tiger.

definition_zh: 比喻在关键处用精辟的词句点明要旨，使内容更加生动有力。
definition_en: To add the pupils to a painted dragon; the finishing touch that brings a work to life.
example_zh: 演讲最后加上这个例子，真是画龙点睛。
example_en: Adding that example at the end of the speech was the finishing touch that brought it to life.

definition_zh: 比喻对不懂道理的人讲道理，白费口舌；也用来讥笑说话的人不看对象。
definition_en: To play the lute to a cow; to talk over the head of one's audience.
example_zh: 跟完全不懂音乐的人大谈交响乐，简直是对牛弹琴。
example_en: Talking at length about symphonies to someone who knows nothing about music is like playing the lute to a cow.

definition_zh: 比喻因疑神疑鬼而引起恐惧，自己惊扰自己。
definition_en: To mistake a bow's reflection in a cup for a snake; to be frightened by purely imaginary fears.
example_zh: 那只是一场误会，别再杯弓蛇影，自己吓自己了。
example_en: It was just a misunderstanding; stop frightening yourself over imaginary fears.

definition_zh: 比喻没有真才实学的人混在行家里面充数，或以次充好。
definition_en: To fill a seat in the orchestra without knowing how to play; to be a mere number in a group.
example_zh: 团队里难免有人滥竽充数，但关键时刻还是要靠真本事。
example_en: Every team has someone just filling a seat, but when it really counts, only true ability matters.

definition_zh: 比喻做事之前已经有通盘的考虑和成功的把握。
definition_en: To have a finished bamboo picture already in mind; to have a well-thought-out plan and full confidence.
example_zh: 面对记者的提问，他胸有成竹，一一作答。
example_en: Facing the reporters' questions, he answered each one with calm confidence, a clear plan already in mind.

definition_zh: 比喻违背事物发展的规律，急于求成，反而把事情弄糟。
definition_en: To pull up seedlings to help them grow; to spoil things by being overeager for quick results.
example_zh: 孩子的成长有自身的规律，拔苗助长只会适得其反。
example_en: Children grow at their own pace; forcing their growth will only backfire.

definition_zh: 比喻用空想或虚假的许诺来安慰自己，解决不了实际问题。
definition_en: To quench one's thirst by thinking of plums; to console oneself with empty promises.
example_zh: 光说发奖金却不兑现，那只是望梅止渴。
example_en: Promising bonuses without ever paying them is nothing but quenching thirst by thinking of plums.

definition_zh: 比喻用空想来安慰自己，解决不了实际的困难。
definition_en: To draw cakes to stave off hunger; to feed on illusions instead of real solutions.
example_zh: 计划再美好，不落实也只是画饼充饥。
example_en: However beautiful the plan, without action it's just drawing cakes to stave off hunger.

definition_zh: 比喻只会空谈理论，不联系实际，不能解决具体问题。
definition_en: To be an armchair strategist; all talk and no practical ability.
example_zh: 管理不能只纸上谈兵，要到一线去了解实际情况。
example_en: Management can't just be armchair strategy; you have to go to the front line and see what's really happening.

definition_zh: 比喻在行家面前卖弄本领，不自量力（含自谦或讥讽之意）。
definition_en: To brandish one's axe at Master Lu Ban's door; to show off meagre skills before an expert.
example_zh: 在专家面前谈这个话题，我不过是班门弄斧。
example_en: Talking about this in front of experts, I'm merely showing off my meagre skills before a master.

definition_zh: 比喻一味模仿别人，不仅学不到本事，反而把自己原有的也丢了。
definition_en: To imitate the gait of Handan so blindly that one forgets how to walk; to lose one's own strengths through mindless copying.
example_zh: 学别人要结合自身特点，邯郸学步只会连自己的长处也丢了。
example_en: When learning from others, adapt to your own strengths; imitating blindly will cost you even what you were good at.

definition_zh: 比喻胡乱模仿，效果适得其反。
definition_en: Like Dongshi imitating Xishi's frown; to copy others clumsily and make things worse.
example_zh: 模仿成功产品要抓本质，东施效颦只会弄巧成拙。
example_en: Imitating a successful product means capturing its essence; copying its surface will only backfire.

definition_zh: 比喻一时虽然受到损失，但也许会因此得到好处，坏事在一定条件下可以变成好事。
definition_en: Like the old man on the frontier who lost his horse; a loss may turn out to be a blessing in disguise.
example_zh: 这次落选未必是坏事，塞翁失马，焉知非福。
example_en: Missing out this time may not be a bad thing — a loss can turn out to be a blessing in disguise.

definition_zh: 比喻只顾眼前利益、不顾身后隐患，或目光短浅、只盯着眼前的得失。
definition_en: Like the mantis stalking the cicada, unaware of the oriole behind; to fixate on immediate gain and miss the danger lurking behind.
example_zh: 做事要考虑长远，别只顾眼前，螳螂捕蝉，黄雀在后。
example_en: Think long-term and don't fixate on what's in front of you — while the mantis stalks the cicada, the oriole lurks behind.

definition_zh: 比喻两方争斗不下，结果两败俱伤，让第三方得利。
definition_en: Like the snipe and the clam locked in a stalemate, to the fisherman's benefit; mutual strife that only helps a third party.
example_zh: 你们两家再这样斗下去，只会鹬蚌相争，让第三家得利。
example_en: If your two companies keep fighting, you'll only let a third party reap the benefit.

definition_zh: 比喻有限的一点本领已经用完，再也没有办法了。
definition_en: Like the Guizhou donkey that has exhausted its tricks; to have run out of ideas and means.
example_zh: 他的招数都用完了，已经黔驴技穷。
example_en: He has used up all his tricks and run out of ideas.

definition_zh: 比喻没有眼光，取舍不当，只看重外表而丢掉了真正有价值的东西。
definition_en: To keep the casket and return the pearl; to value the packaging over the substance.
example_zh: 买东西要看重实用，别买椟还珠，光图包装好看。
example_en: When buying things, value usefulness over fancy packaging — don't keep the casket and return the pearl.

definition_zh: 比喻只相信教条，不顾实际情况，固执呆板、不知变通。
definition_en: Like the man of Zheng who trusted his foot measurements more than his own feet; rigid adherence to rules over reality.
example_zh: 规则是死的，人是活的，不能像郑人买履那样只信尺码不信脚。
example_en: Rules are rigid but people are flexible; don't be like the man of Zheng who trusted his measurements more than his own feet.

definition_zh: 比喻言行或说法前后不一致，互相抵触。
definition_en: To contradict oneself; self-contradictory. (From the merchant who praised his spears and shields with claims that cancelled each other out.)
example_zh: 他前后说法不一致，明显的自相矛盾。
example_en: His statements don't line up — a clear case of self-contradiction.

definition_zh: 比喻为根本不会发生或不必要的事情担忧。
definition_en: Like the man of Qi who feared the sky would fall; to worry over imaginary troubles.
example_zh: 事情还没发生，别杞人忧天，先把眼前的做好。
example_en: Nothing has happened yet; stop worrying over imaginary troubles and focus on what's in front of you.

definition_zh: 比喻做事有顽强的毅力，不怕困难，坚持到底。
definition_en: Like the Foolish Old Man who moved the mountains; steadfast perseverance in the face of great difficulty.
example_zh: 只要有愚公移山的精神，再大的困难也能克服。
example_en: With the perseverance of the Foolish Old Man who moved the mountains, any difficulty can be overcome.

definition_zh: 比喻意志坚定，不畏艰难，坚持不懈地努力。
definition_en: Like the Jingwei bird tirelessly filling the sea with twigs and pebbles; unwavering determination against impossible odds.
example_zh: 他多年坚持做公益，这种精卫填海的精神令人敬佩。
example_en: His years of persistence in charity work — in the spirit of Jingwei filling the sea — are truly admirable.
